A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Variational Best-of-N Alignment and retain the same core method and sentiment experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original IMDB sentiment-generation experiments, Monte Carlo estimation tests, and appendix comparisons involving the lower-bound objective and BoN-SFT.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds preprocessing-efficiency measurements, Reddit summarization experiments, distribution-shift evaluations, and generated-summary examples.

M1.justification: The reverse-KL objective, PPO optimization, and single-sample inference remain unchanged. For the new summarization task, Section 6 introduces a procedural adaptation: fitting an exponential function, -a exp(-bx), to estimated log F using nonlinear least squares. v1 describes only the empirical Monte Carlo estimator.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates controlled positive-sentiment generation on IMDB. v2 retains this coverage and adds Reddit TL;DR summarization, training on relationship-related subreddits and evaluating both those subreddits and other, held-out subreddit domains.

E2.justification: The sentiment comparisons retain BoN, PPO, DPO, BoNBoN, and appendix BoN-SFT. vBoN-L2 is renamed vBoN-L without changing its objective. Summarization reuses existing alignment comparators and the supervised reference model, labeled SFT. Newly discussed BOND is not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: The original IMDB splits and hyperparameter sweeps remain unchanged. New summarization protocols use a Pythia-2.8B policy and training reward model, a separate Pythia-6.9B evaluator, 10,000 optimization episodes, 200 CDF samples, equally sized in-distribution/out-of-distribution test groups, and four sampling temperatures. The new efficiency study fixes N=10 and varies M from 2 to 256.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained CDF-estimation tests and lower-bound/BoN-SFT comparisons, Section 5.2 tests how CDF sample size affects preprocessing time and downstream performance. Section 6 adds temperature sensitivity and held-out-subreddit generalization tests. Table 2 and Appendix I provide qualitative summary comparisons across temperatures.

E5.justification: v2 adds mean and standard-deviation reporting for three-seed efficiency experiments and three-seed summarization sampling in Figures 4–5. The original sentiment sweep seed counts and Table 1's Kolmogorov–Smirnov testing remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish increased replication of those retained experiments.

E6.justification: The original sentiment curves, Pareto percentages, and Table 1 values are retained. New results include summarization reward/win-rate curves favoring vBoN over PPO at lower temperatures and preprocessing measurements of 10 minutes for M=32 versus 74 minutes for M=256. New summary examples include Table 2's rewards of 6.79 for vBoN, 4.59 for PPO, and 9.18 for BoN.

T1.justification: The relationship between the lower bounds is substantively corrected. v1's Theorem 3 states J >= L1 >= L2; v2 renames L2 to L and establishes J >= L >= L1 through Theorems 2 and 4. Appendix D replaces the derivation of J >= L and adds a separate ordering proof. The original L1 formula and theorem are retained in the appendix.

C1.justification: The central contribution—approximating BoN through reverse-KL fine-tuning with N-fold inference-throughput savings—is retained. The abstract and introduction extend the empirical claims to summarization, including higher average rewards and win rates than KL-constrained RL and high rewards across sampling temperatures. The sentiment claim is refined toward Pareto-front performance.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of computational cost and applicability: CDF preprocessing is treated as an amortizable overhead, and similar in-distribution/out-of-distribution results are interpreted as evidence of generalization. It discusses temperature-dependent performance and possible learned CDF approximations. Section 3 also qualifies v1's asserted outlier insensitivity to 'may be less sensitive.'

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, Algorithm 1, CDF-precomputation details, vLLM and A100-40GB timing information, summarization checkpoint identifiers, and a detailed PPO hyperparameter table. These substantially expand reproducibility information. Some regularization documentation remains ambiguous: Section 6 specifies N=100, while the appendix table lists beta=0.05 for both vBoN and KL-constrained RL.

R1.justification: New Appendix A expands positioning around BoN applications, inference scaling, and distillation, including a substantive comparison with Sessa et al.'s BOND. v2 also acknowledges Beirami et al.'s derivation of the BoN probability mass function and adds theoretical and implementation references. These extend the research context beyond bibliographic formatting changes.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies notation and background explanations, streamlines Section 4 around the tighter bound, and moves the other bound to the appendix. It renames Experiments to Sentiment Control and updates authorship and publication headers. Much of the original introduction, method exposition, sentiment discussion, and conclusion remains closely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds the method schematic, efficiency plot, summarization temperature plots, notation and hyperparameter tables, pseudocode, and summary-example tables. Original Figures 1–4 are largely retained as Figures 2, 3, 6, and 7. Table 2's example is redisplayed as Table 5, rather than constituting another independent result.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's single sentiment task through summarization with a separate evaluation reward model, held-out domains, temperature sweeps, and reported variability. It also measures previously unquantified preprocessing costs and corrects the lower-bound ordering and proof, addressing important empirical and theoretical weaknesses. Expanded implementation documentation further improves usefulness. The unresolved summarization regularization detail limits reproducibility but does not outweigh these gains.
